findings.description: Scope detection logic sets normal_failed=1 when ANY scope query fails, which later forces FLATHUB_STATE=unknown even when another scope successfully found flathub enabled
findings.counterexample: Flatpak installed; system scope remote-list fails (permission/timeout), user scope has flathub enabled → reports 'unknown' instead of 'enabled' with scope 'user'

findings.description: Same as claim 1: user scope detection corrupted by system scope failure
findings.counterexample: System scope query fails, user scope has flathub enabled → FLATHUB_ENABLED=1 but FLATHUB_STATE=unknown

findings.description: Both-scope detection fails when either scope query fails; scopes variable only accumulates on success but normal_failed poisons final state
findings.counterexample: Flathub enabled in both scopes, but system query fails → scopes=' user' but STATE=unknown

findings.description: Configured-but-disabled check (--show-disabled) only runs if ALL normal queries succeeded AND none found flathub; partial failure skips disabled detection entirely
findings.counterexample: System query fails, user query succeeds with no flathub → should detect 'disabled' or 'not-configured' for user, but --show-disabled check skipped → STATE=unknown

findings.description: Config file fallback only triggers when flatpak binary is absent (bin=""); if binary exists but all remote-list calls fail, falls back to 'unknown' instead of probing config files
findings.counterexample: Flatpak binary present but segfaults on remote-list → STATE=unknown instead of probing ~/.local/share/flatpak/repo/config

findings.description: Config parser regex requires section header on single line; fails to match '[remote "flathub"] # comment' (inline comments)
findings.counterexample: Config with '[remote "flathub"] # my flathub' → not detected as configured

findings.description: Enabled value parsing doesn't handle quoted values (enabled="false") and misses 'enable' alias; quoted false becomes malformed
findings.counterexample: enabled="false" → value parsed as '"false"' → treated as malformed → disabled (fail-safe works but incorrectly flags malformed)

findings.description: Any non-empty line inside [remote "flathub"] section marks malformed (line 333), including valid keys like 'url=', 'gpg-verify=' → triggers UNKNOWN state
findings.counterexample: Config with '[remote "flathub"]\nurl=https://flathub.org/repo' → _flathub_cf_malformed=1 → FLATHUB_STATE=unknown instead of enabled/disabled

findings.description: Lazy cache uses _FLATHUB_DETECTED flag but flathub_detect runs fresh every explicit call; _flathub_ensure suppresses errors with '|| true' potentially caching garbage; double-detection when caller uses both flathub_detect and accessors
findings.counterexample: Caller calls flathub_detect() then flathub_enabled() → detection runs twice; if first detection fails but || true masks it, cached garbage persists

findings.description: Cache hash uses colon-separated fields; if any field contains a colon, hash becomes ambiguous (collision). djb2 fallback uses bash arithmetic which handles overflow but colon ambiguity remains
findings.counterexample: FLATHUB_STATE='enabled:FLATHUB_SCOPE=system' vs 'FLATHUB_STATE=enabled:FLATHUB_SCOPE=system:' (empty bin) could produce same hash with djb2

findings.description: Binary allowlist misses common NixOS paths (/run/current-system/sw/bin/flatpak, /nix/var/nix/profiles/system/sw/bin/flatpak); validation executes binary with --version (defeats 'never executed' claim)
findings.counterexample: Standard NixOS flatpak at /run/current-system/sw/bin/flatpak → validation fails → binary rejected → falls back to config files which also fail NixOS paths

findings.description: TOCTOU mitigation validates original path, then canonicalizes with realpath -m (resolves missing), then validates canonical; but stat() calls use original path $f (follows symlinks), so mtime/inode check is on target not symlink; race between stat and read
findings.counterexample: Symlink /var/lib/flatpak/repo/config -> /tmp/legit; stat 1 gets legit inode; attacker swaps symlink to /tmp/evil (same inode via hardlink + touch -r); read gets evil content; stat 2 same inode/mtime → check passes

findings.description: NixOS config path allowlist only permits /nix/store/*/flatpak/* but NixOS flatpak configs typically at /etc/flatpak/installations.d/ or /nix/store/.../etc/flatpak/; binary allowlist also misses NixOS paths
findings.counterexample: Standard NixOS flatpak installation → both binary and config validation fail → complete detection failure

findings.description: Homebrew detection only checks standard prefixes (/opt/homebrew, /usr/local); custom Homebrew prefixes not detected; flatpak on macOS is rare and user-session based, system config concept doesn't apply
findings.counterexample: Homebrew installed at /custom/brew → _flathub_check_homebrew returns 1 → custom paths rejected

findings.description: Correctly uses type -P for flatpak lookup (line 465); inconsistent with line 120 using command -v for realpath but not security-critical
findings.counterexample: None - this claim holds

findings.description: TOCTOU mitigation has gaps: realpath -m canonicalizes missing files; stat uses original path (follows symlinks); race between first stat and while-read open; theoretical collision if attacker matches inode+mtime
findings.counterexample: Attacker replaces config file between stat and read with file having same inode (hardlink) and mtime (touch -r) → TOCTOU check passes

findings.description: Scope normalization handles leading space correctly but line 530 forces FLATHUB_SCOPE=system when enabled but scope empty; inconsistent with documented 'empty' return for flathub_scope()
findings.counterexample: Config fallback detects enabled but scope_list empty (shouldn't happen but possible) → flathub_scope returns empty but FLATHUB_SCOPE forced to 'system'

findings.description: flathub_scope_enabled returns 1 for both 'not enabled in scope' and 'error' (binary missing, validation failed, remote-list failed); caller cannot distinguish
findings.counterexample: Caller checks flathub_scope_enabled system → gets 1; cannot tell if flathub disabled in system scope vs flatpak binary missing

findings.description: Source guard 'return 0 2>/dev/null || exit 0' kills shell if sourced in 'bash -c ". file"' (return fails, exit 0 executes); readonly variable assignment at line 120 could be empty in set -u
findings.counterexample: bash -c '. fx-flathub-detect.sh' → shell exits immediately

findings.description: Direct execution guard correctly exits with code 2
findings.counterexample: None - this claim holds

findings.description: Double-source guard works correctly with _FLATHUB_DETECT_SOURCED
findings.counterexample: None - this claim holds

findings.description: State machine priority wrong: normal_failed=1 (partial failure) overrides found_enabled=1 → STATE=unknown even when flathub definitively found enabled in another scope
findings.counterexample: System query fails, user query finds flathub enabled → FLATHUB_ENABLED=1 but FLATHUB_STATE=unknown

findings.description: Authoritative 'no flathub' from successful remote-list is respected (fallback only when no binary), but partial failure (one scope ok, one failed) triggers UNKNOWN instead of respecting the authoritative answer from the successful scope
findings.counterexample: System query fails, user query returns authoritative 'no flathub' → should be not-configured, gets unknown

findings.description: Path redaction incomplete: /home/user/.local/share/flatpak/repo/config → <HOME>/.local/share/flatpak/repo/config (partial); only exact /var/lib/flatpak/repo/config redacted, not variants
findings.counterexample: User home at /home/alice → debug shows '<HOME>/.local/share/flatpak/repo/config' revealing directory structure

steelman: The library correctly uses type -P for binary lookup (claim 15), avoiding alias/function resolution
Double-source guard and direct-execution rejection are solid (claims 20, 21)
Config file parsing correctly handles case-insensitive enabled=false values and fails safe to disabled for unrecognized values (claim 7)
The detection ladder (binary → remote-list → config fallback) is architecturally sound and documented
TOCTOU mitigation attempt with dual validation (original + canonical) and mtime/inode checking shows security awareness
Scope normalization logic correctly handles space-joined lists and maps to stable vocabulary
Debug redaction covers major sensitive path patterns (home, nix store, homebrew)
Cache integrity verification with hash comparison provides defense-in-depth against cache poisoning
NixOS/Homebrew detection via os-release and brew binary presence is reasonable for common cases
All globals are always written, making the library safe for set -u callers (mostly)
counterArgument: The CRITICAL flaw in claims 1-3, 22: normal_failed poisoning makes the library unreliable whenever ANY scope query fails, which is common in real environments (permissions, timeouts, transient errors)
The config parser's malformed flag (claim 8) is triggered by VALID flatpak config keys (url, gpg-verify, etc.), making config fallback actively harmful
Binary allowlist (claim 11) is incomplete for NixOS and other distros, causing false negatives on valid installations
The '|| true' error suppression in _flathub_ensure (claim 9) masks real failures and can cache garbage state
TOCTOU mitigation (claim 16) has fundamental races: realpath -m on missing files, stat on symlink target not symlink, window between stat and read
State machine (claim 22) prioritizes 'unknown' over 'enabled' when partial failure occurs, violating the documented semantics that enabled in ANY scope = enabled
Cache hash (claim 10) uses ambiguous colon-separated format vulnerable to collision
Source guard (claim 19) can kill the shell when sourced in non-standard contexts (bash -c, eval)
flathub_scope_enabled (claim 18) conflates 'not enabled' with 'error', breaking caller logic
Path redaction (claim 24) leaks directory structure under home directory
